Reddit's moderator interface is pretty basic and doesn't give mods the information they need to properly moderate their subreddits. We could learn from reddit's mistakes and build in additional moderator tools to help avoid that problem.

Let moderators see who up/downvoted each comment. If someone goes on a downvote brigade, it would be nice to know who it was. On reddit, this information is visible only to admins.

If a user is banned from a subverse, they should no longer be allowed to up/down vote stuff in that subverse. On reddit, getting banned from a subreddit only prevents you from posting there, but you can still vote on stuff to your heart's content, which leads to toxic subreddits where every new post or comment gets instantly downvoted by a ton of bitter former subscribers who were banned for one reason or another. It would be cool if a banned user also lost their ability to vote on the subverse from which they were banned.

Let moderators see who up/downvoted each comment.

I think this is a problem from a privacy perspective. People may be less willing to vote at all if they think that other users will be able to see what they voted on.
